extracted.intended_audience: machine-learning researchers and engineers using the GSM8K dataset or training/evaluating language models on grade-school math word problems
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for using the GSM8K grade-school math dataset (file formats, annotations, train/test split) and for training/sampling models that use the dataset (calculator annotations, solution extraction, socratic variants, example model solutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset size and split
rubrics_metrics.description: GSM8K consists of 8.5K high quality grade school math problems created by human problem writers. We segmented these into 7.5K training problems and 1K test problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems are provided as raw data files: grade_school_math/data/train.jsonl and grade_school_math/data/test.jsonl; each line corresponds to a single problem (json dictionary with "question" and "answer" keys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem complexity / target solver
rubrics_metrics.description: These problems take between 2 and 8 steps to solve, and solutions primarily involve performing a sequence of elementary calculations using basic arithmetic operations (+ - / * ) to reach the final answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bright middle school student should be able to solve every problem. Use this as a guide for acceptable conceptual complexity and expected solution style (elementary arithmetic sequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data file format (jsonl with question/answer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each line of the data files is a json dictionary with a "question" key and an "answer" key.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The "answer" field is formatted with calculation annotations and the final numeric solution as the final line preceded by the token '####' (see Solution Extracting). Use dataset.py:is_correct for an example of parsing/extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer formatting: final numeric solution token
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer is formatted such that it uses calculation annotations and so that the final numeric solution is the final line of the solution, preceded by '####'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To extract the final numeric solution for a question, parse the completion and extract the numeric value immediately following the '####' token. Example parsing code is shown in dataset.py:is_correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation annotations (calculator integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training data includes calculation annotations (e.g., strings like '<<50*3=150>>') to help models use a calculator and reduce arithmetic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At training time, finetune on this language data as-is. At test time, a calculator will override sampling when the model chooses to use these annotations. Example implementation of calculator sampling is in calculator.py.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removing calculator annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would like to remove the calculator annotations from the dataset, remove any string that starts with '<<' and ends with '>>'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the simple method to produce a dataset without embedded calculation annotations; be aware doing so will remove the signals used by calculator-based sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socratic dataset variant
rubrics_metrics.description: A modified solution format that injects automatically generated 'Socratic subquestions' before each step is available (train_socratic.jsonl and test_socratic.jsonl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Socratic subquestions were generated by conditioning on each ground-truth step using a model finetuned for this task (on ~800 examples). Each step in the solution was prefixed by the model-generated subquestion; steps were otherwise left untouched. This format was investigated but not used in the paper's experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provided model solution outputs and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: For each test question, the repository provides model-generated solutions from 6B finetuning, 6B verification, 175B finetuning and 175B verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These model solutions are in grade_school_math/data/example_model_solutions.jsonl and can be viewed with python view_model_solutions.py. Note: earlier calculator implementation bugs caused calculator failures in roughly 1% of model samples; those samples have not been regenerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculator sampling implementation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The core calculator sampling logic is implemented in calculator.py:sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provided implementation is inefficient: it does not support batches and does not cache activations from previous tokens. Consider these limitations if adapting for large-scale sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage / training examples (illustrative only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository includes basic example code to train a GPT2-sized model and use the calculator in the sampling process (python train.py and python sample.py).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pipeline is included for illustrative purposes only and was not used for the paper's experiments; treat it as an example starting point rather than an experimental recipe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation requirement / recommended citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The README supplies a BibTeX entry to cite the dataset: @article{cobbe2021gsm8k, title={Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems}, ...}
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please use the provided BibTeX entry when citing the dataset in publications or reports.
